s: A company is migrating mobile banking applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. Backend service applications run in an on-premises data center. The data center has an AWS Direct Connect connection into AWS. The applications that run in the VPC need to resolve DNS requests to an on-premises Active Directory domain that runs in the data center. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
o: Provision a set of EC2 instances across two Availability Zones in the VPC as caching DNS servers to resolve DNS queries from the application servers within the VPC.
Provision an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone. Configure NS records that point to on-premises DNS servers.
Create DNS endpoints by using Amazon Route 53 Resolver Add conditional forwarding rules to resolve DNS namespaces between the on-premises data center and the VPC.
Provision a new Active Directory domain controller in the VPC with a bidirectional trust between this new domain and the on-premises Active Directory domain.
e: To enable EC2 instances in the VPC to resolve on-premises Active Directory DNS queries with minimal administrative overhead: l Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints: These allow on-premises DNS servers to forward DNS queries to AWS l Route 53 Resolver rules: Create conditional forwarding rules that redirect queries for the on-premises domain to the on-premises DNS servers via the Direct Connect connection This approach requires no manual DNS configuration on individual EC2 instances and leverages the existing Direct Connect connection. It's more automated than manually configuring /etc/resolv.conf on each instance or running self-managed DNS servers. The Route 53 Resolver service handles the DNS resolution intelligently based on domain rules.

w.y: Resolving an on-premises AD domain from a VPC with 'LEAST administrative overhead' is the job of Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints and forwarding rules. They are managed and highly available, with no servers to run.

o.A: Self-managed DNS servers add patching and HA work.
o.B: A private hosted zone with NS records does not delegate to on-premises DNS servers.
o.C: Correct: Resolver endpoints with conditional forwarding rules.
o.D: A new domain controller and trust is far more effort than DNS forwarding.
